decisions.reason: Cleaning soap is closely related to the firm's existing wood-floor maintenance and surface-treatment knowledge, so early market feedback can be absorbed and used to refine rather than withdraw it.
Maintenance oil builds directly on the firm's core competence in wooden floors and finishing systems, and as a multi-model line it can be adjusted without needing to exit the category.
A care product for oiled wood floors fits the firm's installed base and technical advisory capabilities, making it a commercially learnable extension with good absorptive fit.

A moisture-protection underlay is somewhat less central than the floor itself but still part of a flooring system the firm already sells and supports, so it is more likely to be improved than dropped.

High-density underlay foam is an adjacent accessory where the firm can learn through installers and partners, though its material base is a bit less tied to core wood-processing know-how than finishes or parquet.

Oak parquet flooring is squarely within the firm's deepest manufacturing, design, and sales knowledge, so in a growing market a recently launched line would very likely be retained and developed further.
